items.title: Al Gallodoro Interview, 1966-05-10
items.q: Mr. Jansen, I've heard this many, many times. Where trumpet players will say to the conductor...

ctx.x: I'll call you Al. Oh, I want you to. Okay. And we'll talk. He's going to play a little bit, talk a bit. And those of you in high school will be led out by our college, we have some college boys in charge, showing where to go.

I think make the Coo sound exactly like a Coo, like a 2. Of course you would never use it that slow. You'd only use it when a single tongue becomes too fast. That's the regular Tukutu. Now the triple tongue would be Tukutu Tukutu Tukutu. Mr. Jansen, I've heard this many, many times. Where trumpet players will say to the conductor, could you take it a little faster because it's too hard to double tongue at the speed. I have never had this trumbler. I don't understand. Is it different on a brass instrument? No,…
Sometimes we feel the tempo is too slow for double tongue or triple tongue. In other words, when you get to an in-between tempo, you know what I mean? Yes.
